gap: No result ChatGPT got says how much power a bank just under 100 Wh actually delivers. In ChargerLAB's lab test, the AOHi Future Starship 240W (99.36 Wh) gave out about 79–90 Wh at 15–45 W but tripped its temperature protection after 10 minutes at 140 W, having delivered only about 24 Wh. In Techtest.org's test, the EcoFlow RAPID Pro (99.54 Wh) delivered about 85.5 Wh at that same 28 V/5 A (140 W) load.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT got. FAA PackSafe, the IATA power-bank guidance (cited) and American Airlines' restricted-items page (cited, but it returned HTTP 403 to my fetch) cover the 100 Wh / 160 Wh / airline-approval rules. The FAA and 49 CFR 175.10 results cover the same rules. None of them names a product or gives any measured output. ChatGPT's answer showed no products. Its table only converts mAh to Wh at 3.7 V and treats 27,000 mAh / 99.9 Wh as the target. It never says that a 99 Wh bank delivers only about 75–90 Wh, or that some of these banks cannot hold 140 W.
decides: It changes the lead pick on our current page. The AOHi Future Starship 240W is listed first, but ChargerLAB's test shows it cannot sustain its advertised 140 W, or even 100 W. At 100 W it stopped after 23 minutes with 35.52 Wh delivered. That matters most to the shopper this query brings, who wants the biggest airline-legal bank, usually to run a laptop. In Techtest.org's test the EcoFlow RAPID Pro held 100 W and 140 W loads all the way to empty (84.2 Wh and 85.5 Wh). That makes it the better lead for laptop users, with AOHi demoted to a value or low-power pick. One caveat for the page: these results come from two different labs (ChargerLAB tested in a 25 °C chamber, Techtest.org in a 20–22 °C room). Present them side by side with each lab named, not as one benchmark. For the lower-cost slot, Techtest.org measured 74.3–80.4 Wh from the UGREEN 145W 25,000 mAh and weighed it at 508 g, which suggests that slot doesn't need a full 99 Wh bank.

findings.value: The only bank in the group that would not charge a phone right after an 8 ft drop (it would not turn on until recharged). Full charge took 6 h 39 min. Efficiency was 6% higher in a refrigerator than at room temperature.

unsourced: Anker Prime 27,650 mAh 250W (A1340): a measured Wh delivered from a named lab. ChargerLAB's site search and three web searches found none. Battery Skills' claim of 26,890 mAh at 5 V/3 A was not opened or verified, and a desertcart listing's '~96.7 Wh' comes from an unnamed buyer. Both are left out.
Baseus EnerFill FC41 25,000 mAh 145W: no measured capacity or sustained 140 W test from ChargerLAB, Notebookcheck (launch news only) or any other named reviewer. Only Baseus's rated 91.25 Wh exists.
AOHi Black Warrior 25,200 mAh and AOHi Starship 40,000 mAh: no named lab measurements were searched within the tool budget.
UGREEN Nexode 25,000 mAh 200W (the model Dealectric lists): Techtest.org tested the related Nexode Pro PB728 (200 W, two built-in cables), a different model, so it is not used.
IATA power-bank guidance PDF text: WebFetch returned it as binary and local text extraction was blocked, so I could not quote its wording. Its 100 Wh rule is taken from ChatGPT's answer only.
American Airlines restricted-items page: returned HTTP 403 and could not be read.
